label: first copied token d being fed back (step L+1, first original token d)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at the first step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1), when the fed-back input is d, i.e. the sequence started with d (99.8% of mass). Magnitude is largest for short sequences (L=3-5) and falls steadily with L; at L=9 it is mostly inactive, so the predicate restricts to L<=8 (without the L limit: F1 0.89, mass recall 0.997). Does not fire in the original or delimiter phases, on d at other positions (e.g. a second d at recall_idx 2 gives only weak, rare activation), or on any other first token. Output token, next output, and digit content have no clear effect.

issues: L<=8 cutoff marks a gradual fade, not a sharp boundary. With recall_idx==1 & in_tok==d, precision is 1.0 at L<=4, 0.999 at L<=7, 0.78 at L==8 and 0.25 at L==9. Most of the 614 test false positives are at L=8, and most of the 1156 test misses are tiny activations (0.01-0.07 relative to max) at L=9. Together the misses hold only 0.8% of the activation mass, so this is the magnitude tapering off, not a separate class of inputs.
Claim about weak recall_idx 2 firing checks out: (recall_idx==2)&(in_tok==d) has precision 0.025 and mass recall 0.003.
Off-target firing on other input tokens (h:20, n:6, j:1 of 14226 dev actives) is scattered noise.
Phase claims hold: there is no activation in the original or delimiter phases, and 99.8% of the mass is at recall_idx 1.
The reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.956, R 0.920, F1 0.938, mass recall 0.992.
